g.title: the issuing server does not answer, which is what makes T2 fire

svg.metadata:
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
# Reference figure for genre `sequence` — EXPERIMENTAL GENRE, and one step # further out than the others: this genre HAS NO RENDERER YET. The document # below parses to a complete model and reports zero errors, and drawing it # produces an empty canvas. That is why there is NO sequence.svg beside this # file: an artifact would record a drawing the language does not have. # # What the file is for today is therefore the MODEL, not the picture. It # demonstrates every form of every keyword the genre has, so a reader can see # the whole surface on one page and a coverage tool can count it. # # EVERY line below is outside the compatibility promise: the genre is # experimental (`CONSTRUCT-STATUS-TIERS`'s rule, applied to `sequence`). Read # spec/genres/experimental/sequence.md first — when it exists; until then the # ruled surface is decisions/registry.md and the reading rule is # read/0.4/experimental/sequence.md. figdown 0.4 sequence title "Address lease and renewal"
# `class` declares a meaning ONCE and elements join it with class=. Under this # genre it carries two jobs no keyword does, because both keywords were # refused: it is what `group` would have expressed (a set of participants with # something in common — `SEQUENCE-PARTICIPANT-GROUPING`) and what `lost=` would have expressed (a message # that was sent and not delivered — `UNDELIVERED-MESSAGE-MARKING`). A class earns a legend entry, so # the meaning reaches the reader without a spelling of its own. class dropped "Sent, never delivered"
# ---- lifeline: the participant column ----------------------------------- # `lifeline` is this genre's NODE spelling — the slot `node` fills in block and # `state` fills in statechart (UML 2.5.1 §17.3.3.1). Column order is # DECLARATION order and there is no key that changes it: `flow` and `rank` are # not keywords of this genre, because both axes here are already ordered by the # source and a key that reordered the drawing would make the picture disagree # with the text. # Label optional, exactly as on `node`: `lifeline c` is legal and displays "c". lifeline c "DHCP client" lifeline s "DHCP server"
# ---- message: the line between two participants -------------------------- # `message` is this genre's CONNECTOR spelling (UML 2.5.1 §17.4.4.1) and it # takes all three operators. The trailing quoted string is the message text. # `--` is a LINE ERROR here and legal in every other genre: a Message has a # sending AND a receiving event occurrence, so a direction-less message is not # a thing this domain has. message c -> s "DHCPDISCOVER" message c <- s "DHCPOFFER" message c -> s "DHCPREQUEST" message c <- s "DHCPACK"
# ---- state: a named state OF a lifeline ---------------------------------- # Slot 1 REFERENCES a lifeline; it does not declare an id, because nothing in # this genre refers to a state occurrence. That is the one asymmetry with # `statechart`'s `state`, where slot 1 declares. Slot 2 is the state name and # is MANDATORY — a state occurrence with no name asserts nothing. state c "BOUND"
# ---- fragment + operand: the combined fragment and its compartments ------- # `type=` is MANDATORY and its value is one of the twelve UML # InteractionOperatorKind literals taken whole. UML defaults the attribute to # `seq`; FigDown does not, because a default draws a frame that looks like an # assertion and is not one. fragment renew "renewal cycle" type=loop # An `operand` is a compartment OF a fragment, so its `in=` is MANDATORY. The # quoted string is the guard. operand t1 "at T1 — 0.5x the lease" in=renew
# Membership is `in=`, sense 1: the element this one lives inside. Members must # be CONTIGUOUS in declaration order, because an operand denotes the ORDERED # RUN of the occurrences it contains. message c -> s "DHCPREQUEST (unicast, renewing)" in=t1 class=dropped description="the issuing server does not answer, which is what makes T2 fire"
# `in=` on a `state` too (five acceptors: message, operand, lifeline, state, # fragment). A state occurrence can sit inside a fragment. state c "RENEWING" in=t1
# ONE level of fragment nesting: this fragment sits inside an operand of the # fragment above, and no deeper. Two levels is a line error in v1 — the v0.1 # `group` precedent, and a scope decision rather than a principle. fragment fallback "if T1 expires" type=alt in=t1 operand t2 "at T2 — 0.875x the lease" in=fallback message c <-> s "DHCPREQUEST (broadcast, rebinding)" in=t2
# `in=` on a `lifeline` is the fifth acceptor. It is legal and it is rare: it # says a participant exists only inside a fragment. Not used here, because # both participants exist for the whole exchange — and a reference figure # demonstrates forms that are true of the figure, never forms invented to fill # a table. The form is exercised by conformance fixture 285 instead.
